newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico 10-yr bond to fill out yield curve - experts.
newsitem.headline: Mexico 10-yr bond to fill out yield curve - experts.

text.p: Analysts welcomed Friday the announcement of Mexico's $1.0 billion 10-year global bond issue as a good move to plug a hole in the federal government's yield curve.
"In terms of filling up the yield curve, this issue has been eagerly awaited," said Santander Investment fixed-income analyst Richard Segal.
Merrill Lynch & Co and Salomon Bros Inc said Friday that they will lead manage the issue, the first of the year from Mexico. The issued will be priced and sold next week.
Sovereign debt analysts said that the issue should be warmly received by investors, who have been expecting Mexico to flesh out its yield curve.

"It is a logical part of their curve that they have yet to fill. They have a 30-year, a 20-year and a five-year, so in a sense, it will be very positive," said one debt analyst, who declined to be identified.
Markets prefer to see a complete yield curve for Mexican federal government debt to provide benchmarks for other government agencies, corporates and banks in Mexico.
Ten-year issues figure as benchmarks in both the U.S and Eurobond markets, analysts said.
Analysts say the bond -- like other recent federal issues -- should be attractive to investors.
Moreover, the spread on outstanding longer-denominated Mexican bonds have tightened recently, as have the spreads on Mexican Brady bonds, analysts said.

"I think it will get a fairly good response. In the last month, Mexico has been doing well in terms of performance," said Tulio Vera, emerging markets fixed-income analyst at Bear Stearns. "There is a pretty favourable international liquidity picture."

The federal government has about $1.4 billion in debt coming due in 1997. Including government agency debt, Mexico will need to refinance $4.047 billion of debt in the international capital markets in 1997.
In 1996, the federal government placed five-year, 20-year and 30-year bond issues.
